# Review External acceptance: Intent

This is a PLAN Change for `review`. It ships no code, no Node, no package and no promotion. It prepares Review to be the first subject of an independent External acceptance trial, as the Product PLAN for External KAAL (#978, requirements R1 to R8) proposes and the CPO prefers. It does not claim Review is External-ready: it makes the claim decidable, and names the gaps found while reading Review against R1 to R8.

External KAAL means applying KAAL knowledge in an unrelated repository with no installation, no registration and no Engine. The portfolio view marks Review as the one capability whose Skill states that it stands alone. That is a statement by the author, not yet tested (gap X5). REAL (Review Enhances Agent Leverage) is the reason this matters: an outside Agent that reads Review as plain text should do more reliable review work than the same Agent without it.

- **review/X0.** Review's knowledge for an outside consumer is the Agent Skill `skills/kaal-review/SKILL.md` and its `references/`, read as plain text at a stated version. The Nodes in `payload/` are an optional deeper reference. There is one authoritative text (R1): no parallel External copy is made.
- **review/X1.** Review declares, in one place in the package, what an outside consumer needs to know before acting (R4, R5, R8): that the Skill stands alone; what it depends on (nothing); which optional commands exist (`check-record`, `collect`), what they read and that they write nothing; what effects applying it intends; and that it grants no authority.
- **review/X2.** Review's effects on a target repository are only what the invoker authorizes. Review itself writes nothing to the target. The record is text the invoker may publish (for example as a pull request comment) under the invoker's own authority. The scripts read and print. Knowledge access, intended effects and target authority are kept apart, as R5 requires.
- **review/X3.** A trial names the exact version of the text under test (R6). Review adds no version scheme. At this writing `main` carries the 0.0.1 Skill (no record, no scripts); the structured record and scripts (DO-1, #913) are on `kaal/review`. The two are different artifacts and a trial or a citation must say which.
- **review/X4.** The acceptance run follows the independent bar of #978 section 6: an unrelated repository with no KAAL workspace, no Engine, plain text at the stated version, a real review task chosen by someone other than the author of the Skill, a checker who is not the author and is not primed beyond the text, measured against Review's own stated claims, with every observed effect checked against the effects declared and the authorization given. Testing owns the evidence and verification semantics; Product owns what External-ready means; the Owner decides.
- **review/X5.** What the trial finds returns to Review as Findings, and a confirmed shortfall becomes a Defect with a RED Test Case in Review's own plan. Review does not certify itself External-ready, and adds no gate.

Out of scope here: the entry point and how knowledge becomes reachable and versioned (Product, Engineering and the Owner; promotion routes are the Owner's), a "stands alone" conformance profile (Packaging, #907), npm publication, and any capability other than Review.
